column1: # Sender and subject rules that decide which messages need action.
# Applied to the whole database by imc_tag_apply.sh, so a change here is
# always re-applied to past mail as well. Compare before and after; do not
# judge a rule by reading it.
# Columns are tab separated:
#   tag     the notmuch tag to add. Tags listed here are owned by this file:
#           imc_tag_apply.sh removes them from every message before it
#           re-adds them, so deleting a line really does undo it. Tags that
#           do not appear in this file (done, later, ...) are never touched.
#   field   from, subject, or to
#   regex   case insensitive extended regular expression, matched with ~
#   comment why this rule exists. Future you will ask.
# THIS FILE IS COMMITTED TO GIT and is public. Keep rules here generic
# (subject-based) so that nothing here identifies which bank, which tax
# authority, etc. you use.
# A bare sender rule ("from @bank.example$") was the original plan, but
# real-world testing (two actual U.S. Bank emails) showed it is too broad:
# "Here's the security code you requested" and "Your e-statement is ready."
# come from the exact same sender, yet only the first needs action. Subject
# rules turned out to be both more precise AND privacy-safe here, so they
# are the primary mechanism, not a fallback.
# If a sender truly needs a blanket rule despite that risk (no good subject
# pattern exists), put it in tag_rules.local.tsv instead (gitignored; copy
# tag_rules.local.tsv.template to create it). imc_tag_apply.sh merges both
# files when both are passed to it.
# tag
